questions.questionText: What is the first pillar of Islam?
questions.explanation: Shahadah is the primary foundational pillar of Islam.

questions.questionText: What does the first part of Shahadah testify?
questions.explanation: It declares that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah.

questions.questionText: Who is declared as the final messenger of Allah in Shahadah?
questions.explanation: Shahadah bears witness that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is Allah’s Messenger.

questions.questionText: What does 'La ilaha illallah' mean?
options: There is no god but Allah
questions.explanation: It is the fundamental declaration of Tawheed (Oneness of God).

questions.questionText: Reciting the Shahadah sincerely enters a person into?
questions.explanation: It is the testimony required to become a Muslim.

questions.questionText: What is the original language of the Shahadah?
questions.explanation: The Quran and the Shahadah are in Arabic.

questions.questionText: Who alone deserves to be worshipped according to Shahadah?
questions.explanation: Worship is dedicated strictly to Allah.

questions.questionText: What is the greatest sin in Islam (opposite of Shahadah)?
questions.explanation: Shirk (associating partners with Allah) is the unforgivable sin if not repented.

questions.questionText: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the Messenger and what of Allah?
questions.explanation: Muslims testify he is the slave ('abduhu) and messenger of Allah.

questions.questionText: Belief in the Shahadah must be affirmed by the tongue and?
questions.explanation: True faith requires affirmation by the tongue and belief in the heart.

questions.questionText: How many daily obligatory prayers are prescribed in Islam?
questions.explanation: Muslims perform 5 obligatory prayers daily.

questions.questionText: Which prayer is offered right before sunrise?
questions.explanation: Fajr prayer is offered before dawn.

questions.questionText: What is the required ablution before Salah called?
questions.explanation: Wudu is required for ritual purity before prayer.

questions.questionText: Which direction do Muslims face during Salah?
questions.explanation: Muslims face the Kaaba in Makkah.

questions.questionText: What is the midday prayer called?
questions.explanation: Dhuhr is the prayer performed just after midday.

questions.questionText: What is the call to prayer called in Islam?
questions.explanation: The Adhan is called out to notify Muslims that it is time for prayer.

questions.questionText: Which prayer is performed just after sunset?
questions.explanation: Maghrib is the fourth obligatory prayer, prayed immediately after sunset.

questions.questionText: What is the weekly congregational prayer on Friday called?
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah replaces the Dhuhr prayer on Fridays and includes a sermon.

questions.questionText: What do we say when starting the prayer?
questions.explanation: Takbeer (Allahu Akbar) is used to commence the prayer.

questions.questionText: What is the physical act of prostration in prayer called?
questions.explanation: Sujud (Sajdah) is prostrating with the forehead touching the ground.

questions.questionText: What is the standard rate of Zakat on accumulated wealth?
questions.explanation: The standard Zakat rate is 2.5% on qualifying wealth held for a year.

questions.questionText: What is the minimum wealth threshold for Zakat called?
questions.explanation: Nisab is the minimum wealth required before Zakat becomes obligatory.

questions.questionText: Which group of people is eligible to receive Zakat?
questions.explanation: Surah At-Tawbah verse 60 lists the eligible categories for Zakat.

questions.questionText: What is the literal meaning of the word 'Zakat'?
questions.explanation: Zakat purifies one's remaining wealth and promotes spiritual growth.

questions.questionText: Is Zakat obligatory on a person who does not meet the Nisab?
questions.explanation: Zakat is only obligatory on those whose wealth reaches the Nisab.

questions.questionText: What is voluntary charity called in Islam?
questions.explanation: Sadaqah can be given at any time and in any amount.

questions.questionText: Which item is subject to Zakat?
questions.explanation: Personal necessities are exempt, but hoarded precious metals are subject to Zakat.

questions.questionText: When is Zakat al-Fitr mandatory to be given?
questions.explanation: It must be given before the Eid prayer at the end of Ramadan.

questions.questionText: Can Zakat be given to build a mosque?
options: No, it is for specific categories of people
questions.explanation: Zakat is primarily for the 8 specific categories mentioned in the Quran.

questions.questionText: How long must wealth be held above Nisab before Zakat is due?
questions.explanation: One full Hijri year (Hawl) must pass on the qualifying wealth.

questions.questionText: In which month is mandatory fasting observed?
questions.explanation: Fasting is mandatory during the month of Ramadan.

questions.questionText: What is the pre-dawn meal before starting a fast called?
questions.explanation: Suhoor is eaten before dawn to prepare for the fast.

questions.questionText: What is the meal eaten at sunset to break the fast called?
questions.explanation: Iftar is the meal eaten to break the fast at Maghrib.

questions.questionText: At what time does the fast begin?
questions.explanation: Fasting begins at true dawn.

questions.questionText: Who is exempt from fasting during Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Those who are ill or traveling are permitted to break their fast and make it up later.

questions.questionText: What is the special night prayer in Ramadan called?
questions.explanation: Tarawih prayers are held in congregation every night in Ramadan.

questions.questionText: What breaks a fast?
questions.explanation: Intentionally eating or drinking nullifies the fast.

questions.questionText: What is the Night of Power called?
questions.explanation: Laylatul Qadr is better than a thousand months.

questions.questionText: Which festival marks the end of Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated on the 1st of Shawwal.

questions.questionText: Fasting teaches Muslims what virtue?
questions.explanation: The primary goal of fasting is to attain Taqwa.

questions.questionText: In which holy city is Hajj performed?
questions.explanation: Hajj is performed in and around Makkah.

questions.questionText: On which day of Dhul Hijjah does standing at Mount Arafah occur?
questions.explanation: Standing at Arafah (Wuquf) takes place on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah.

questions.questionText: What is the sacred state required for performing Hajj?
questions.explanation: Ihram is the sacred state entered into before performing Hajj or Umrah.

questions.questionText: Circling the Kaaba is known as?
questions.explanation: Tawaf involves circumambulating the Kaaba 7 times.

questions.questionText: How many times must a pilgrim perform Tawaf around the Kaaba?
questions.explanation: It is required to circle the Kaaba 7 times.

questions.questionText: Walking between the hills of Safa and Marwa is called?
questions.explanation: Sa'i commemorates Hajar's search for water.

questions.questionText: Stoning the pillars in Mina is known as?
questions.explanation: Rami al-Jamarat is the stoning of the devil.

questions.questionText: Which animal is commonly sacrificed during Hajj?
questions.explanation: Livestock like sheep, goats, cows, or camels are sacrificed.

questions.questionText: Which Eid is celebrated during Hajj?
questions.explanation: Eid al-Adha is the festival of sacrifice.

questions.questionText: How many times is Hajj obligatory for a capable Muslim in their lifetime?
questions.explanation: It is mandatory once in a lifetime if one has the physical and financial means.

questions.questionText: Tawheed is divided into how many main categories by scholars?
questions.explanation: Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah, Uluhiyyah, and Asma was-Sifat.

questions.questionText: What does Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah mean?
questions.explanation: It means believing Allah is the sole Creator, Provider, and Sustainer.

questions.questionText: Which form of Shirk completely takes a person out of the fold of Islam?
questions.explanation: Major Shirk nullifies faith.

questions.questionText: Belief in Allah's names and attributes falls under which category?
questions.explanation: It relates to Allah's unique Names and Attributes.

questions.questionText: What was the core message of all the Prophets?
questions.explanation: Every prophet was sent with the message of worshipping Allah alone.

questions.questionText: Which Surah is considered equivalent to one-third of the Quran due to its focus on Tawheed?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas purely describes the oneness of Allah.

questions.questionText: What is the condition of 'Yaqeen' regarding the Shahadah?
questions.explanation: Yaqeen means having absolute certainty in the declaration.

questions.questionText: Showing off (Riya) in acts of worship is classified as?
questions.explanation: Riya is considered Shirk al-Asghar (Minor Shirk).

questions.questionText: Who were the first people to be invited to the Shahadah by the Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: He started secretly with his closest associates like Khadijah and Abu Bakr.

questions.questionText: A person who rejects the Sunnah but claims to follow the Quran is violating which part of the Shahadah?
questions.explanation: The second part testifies Muhammad (PBUH) is the Messenger, making his Sunnah binding.

questions.questionText: What is the term for the prostrations performed to correct a mistake in Salah?
questions.explanation: Sujud as-Sahw (Prostration of Forgetfulness) is performed to compensate for certain omissions or additions in prayer.

questions.questionText: How many Takbeers are normally pronounced in the first Rak'ah of Salat al-Janazah (Funeral Prayer)?
questions.explanation: The funeral prayer generally consists of four Takbeers without bowing or prostrating.

questions.questionText: What is the ruling of shortening prayers (Qasr) for a traveler?
questions.explanation: It is a highly recommended Sunnah (concession from Allah) to shorten 4-rak'ah prayers to 2 for travelers.

questions.questionText: Which prayer is performed during a solar or lunar eclipse?
questions.explanation: Kusuf is for solar eclipses and Khusuf is for lunar eclipses.

questions.questionText: What is a 'Sutrah' in the context of Salah?
options: An object placed in front of a praying person
questions.explanation: A Sutrah is an object a worshipper places in front of them to prevent others from passing directly in front of their prayer space.

questions.questionText: How many Sunnah Mu'akkadah (emphasized Sunnah) rak'ahs are there in a day and night?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) mentioned 12 rak'ahs: 2 before Fajr, 4 before Zuhr, 2 after Zuhr, 2 after Maghrib, and 2 after Isha.

questions.questionText: If someone joins the congregation while the Imam is in Ruku, do they count that Rak'ah?
options: Only if they recite Surah Fatihah
questions.explanation: Catching the Ruku with the Imam counts as having caught the complete Rak'ah.

questions.questionText: Which direction did the early Muslims face for prayer before the Qiblah was changed to Makkah?
questions.explanation: The first Qiblah was Bayt al-Maqdis (Al-Aqsa in Jerusalem) before it was changed to the Kaaba.

questions.questionText: What is the prayer for seeking rain called?
questions.explanation: Salat al-Istisqa is specifically performed during times of drought to seek rain from Allah.

questions.questionText: What nullifies the Wudu (ablution) according to general consensus?
options: Deep sleep where awareness is lost
questions.explanation: Deep sleep causes a person to lose physical control, which breaks Wudu.

questions.questionText: How many categories of people are eligible to receive Zakat according to the Quran?
questions.explanation: The Quran lists 8 specific categories of people who can receive Zakat.

questions.questionText: What is the minimum Nisab (threshold) for silver to be eligible for Zakat?
questions.explanation: The Nisab for silver is 595 grams (or 200 dirhams).

questions.questionText: What is the standard Zakat percentage for wealth that has been held for a full lunar year?
questions.explanation: The standard rate is 2.5% (or 1/40th) of qualifying accumulated wealth.

questions.questionText: What is 'Hawl' in the context of Zakat?
questions.explanation: Hawl refers to the passage of one complete lunar year over the wealth.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is Zakat NOT obligatory on?
questions.explanation: Zakat is not paid on items of purely personal use like one's primary residence, clothes, or personal vehicles.

questions.questionText: What is the Zakat on agricultural produce watered naturally (by rain)?
questions.explanation: It is 10% (Ushr) for naturally watered land, and 5% if artificially irrigated.

questions.questionText: Who among the following cannot be given Zakat?
questions.explanation: You cannot give Zakat to your direct dependents (parents, children, spouse) as their maintenance is already your duty.

questions.questionText: What is Zakat al-Fitr?
options: Charity given at the end of Ramadan
questions.explanation: It is a mandatory charity of food given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer.

questions.questionText: What is Rikaz?
options: Buried treasure found in the earth
questions.explanation: Rikaz is hidden or buried treasure, and its Zakat rate is 20% upon finding.

questions.questionText: Can Zakat be given to build a mosque?
options: No, it must go to eligible people directly
Only if the mosque is in debt
questions.explanation: According to the majority of scholars, Zakat is for specific categories of people, whereas general charities (Sadaqah/Waqf) build mosques.

questions.questionText: What is the penalty (Kaffarah) for deliberately breaking a Ramadan fast by eating or drinking without a valid excuse?
questions.explanation: The primary Kaffarah is freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding 60 poor people.

questions.questionText: On which of these days is it strictly Haram (forbidden) to fast?
questions.explanation: Fasting is prohibited on the two days of Eid.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the pre-dawn meal taken before fasting?
questions.explanation: Suhoor is the meal consumed early in the morning before fasting begins.

questions.questionText: Fasting on the Day of Arafah expiates the sins of how many years?
questions.explanation: It expiates the minor sins of the previous year and the coming year.

questions.questionText: What is Fidya in the context of fasting?
options: Compensation paid by those permanently unable to fast
questions.explanation: Fidya is feeding a poor person for every missed fast by someone chronically ill or elderly.

questions.questionText: Fasting 6 days in which Islamic month is equivalent to fasting the whole year when combined with Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Whoever fasts Ramadan, then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if they fasted continually.

questions.questionText: Which historical Islamic event occurred during the month of Ramadan?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Badr took place on the 17th of Ramadan.

questions.questionText: What is 'I'tikaf'?
options: A special food for breaking fast
Secluding oneself in the mosque for worship
questions.explanation: I'tikaf is retreating to the mosque, usually during the last 10 days of Ramadan, to focus solely on worship.

questions.questionText: What does 'Qada' fasting mean?
options: Making up for missed obligatory fasts
questions.explanation: Qada refers to making up missed obligatory fasts of Ramadan at a later date.

questions.questionText: What is the fasting of Prophet Dawud (AS)?
options: Fasting every day of the year
Fasting one day and breaking the fast the next
questions.explanation: Prophet Dawud (AS) used to fast on alternate days, which is highly praised in Hadith.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a recognized type of Hajj?
questions.explanation: The three types are Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj), Qiran (combined), and Ifrad (Hajj only).

questions.questionText: What is a 'Miqat'?
options: A specific boundary where pilgrims must enter Ihram
questions.explanation: Miqat refers to the physical boundaries a pilgrim must not cross without being in a state of Ihram.

questions.questionText: What is 'Talbiyah'?
options: The act of shaving the head
questions.explanation: Talbiyah is the prayer invoked by pilgrims stating their presence for the service of Allah.

questions.questionText: Where do pilgrims spend the night directly after the Day of Arafah?
questions.explanation: After leaving Arafah at sunset, pilgrims travel to Muzdalifah to pray Maghrib and Isha and spend the night.

questions.questionText: The act of Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah) honors the actions of which historical figure?
questions.explanation: It commemorates Hajar's desperate search for water for her infant son Ismail.

questions.questionText: What is 'Tawaf al-Ifadah'?
options: The obligatory Tawaf for Hajj on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah
questions.explanation: Tawaf al-Ifadah (or Tawaf az-Ziyarah) is an essential pillar of Hajj performed after returning from Arafah/Muzdalifah.

questions.questionText: What does 'Rami al-Jamarat' refer to?
questions.explanation: It is the symbolic stoning of the devil performed at three pillars in Mina.

questions.questionText: What does 'Raml' mean during Tawaf?
options: Walking with quick, short steps in the first three circuits
questions.explanation: Raml is the sunnah for men to walk briskly with chests thrust forward during the first three rounds of an initial Tawaf.

questions.questionText: In Hajj, what is 'Dam'?
options: A penalty sacrifice for making a mistake or missing a wajib act
questions.explanation: Dam refers to an expiation (usually sacrificing a sheep) required when a pilgrim violates certain rules of Ihram or misses a mandatory act.

questions.questionText: What is the day of 'Tarwiyah'?
questions.explanation: The 8th of Dhul-Hijjah is called the Day of Tarwiyah (fetching water), when pilgrims move to Mina.

questions.questionText: How many conditions (Shurut) of the Shahadah are universally agreed upon by scholars of Aqeedah?
questions.explanation: They are Knowledge, Certainty, Acceptance, Submission, Truthfulness, Sincerity, and Love.

questions.questionText: The concept of 'Al-Wala wal-Bara' is closely linked to which part of belief?
questions.explanation: It means loyalty to Allah/believers and disavowal of polytheism.

questions.questionText: What does 'Tawheed al-Hakimiyyah' refer to in modern Islamic discourse?
questions.explanation: It refers to the belief that Allah is the ultimate Lawgiver.

questions.questionText: If a person claims a prophet came after Muhammad (PBUH), what is their status?
questions.explanation: Rejecting the finality of Prophethood nullifies Islam.

questions.questionText: According to the Ash'ari and Maturidi schools, how are Allah's attributes understood?
questions.explanation: They affirm the attributes but without anthropomorphism (Tashbih).

questions.questionText: The phrase 'Kufr duna Kufr' (minor disbelief) was famously used by which companion regarding ruling by other than Allah's law?
questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas used this to explain different levels of Kufr.

questions.questionText: What is 'Tawassul'?
options: Seeking a means of nearness to Allah
questions.explanation: Tawassul is using a permissible means to draw close to Allah.

questions.questionText: Which sect historically deviated by claiming that committing a major sin completely expels a person from Islam?
questions.explanation: The Khawarij held the extremist view of Takfir for major sins.

questions.questionText: What is the ruling on one who mocks an established part of the religion out of a joke?
questions.explanation: Mocking Allah, His verses, or His Messenger is an act of Kufr.

questions.questionText: What is 'Ilm al-Kalam'?
questions.explanation: It is the study of Islamic doctrine through dialectical methods.

questions.questionText: According to the majority of scholars (Jumhoor), what is the ruling on a person who abandons Salah entirely out of laziness, but still believes it is obligatory?
options: A major sinner (Fasiq) but still Muslim
questions.explanation: While the Hanbali school considers them a Kafir, the Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanafi schools consider them a major sinner who remains a Muslim.

questions.questionText: What is 'Jam' Taqdeem'?
options: Praying Maghrib and Isha together at the time of Isha
Praying Dhuhr and Asr together at the time of Dhuhr
Praying an extra sunnah before Fard
questions.explanation: Jam' Taqdeem means advancing the later prayer to the time of the earlier one (e.g., Asr at the time of Dhuhr).

questions.questionText: If a person is suffering from 'Istihadah' (continuous non-menstrual bleeding), what must they do to pray?
options: Make a fresh Wudu for every obligatory prayer after its time has entered
Combine all prayers at the end of the day
questions.explanation: They must wash the area, secure it, and make a new Wudu for each prayer time.

questions.questionText: Is Wudu strictly required for 'Sujud al-Tilawah' (prostration of recitation) outside of Salah?
questions.explanation: The four main Madhahib require Wudu for it, though some scholars like Ibn Umar and Ibn Taymiyyah allowed it without.

questions.questionText: In 'Salat al-Khawf' (Prayer of Fear) during battle, how is the prayer typically managed?
options: It is delayed until after the battle
The troops are divided; one group prays with the Imam while the other guards, then they switch
questions.explanation: The Quran explicitly outlines dividing the army so that part of them pray while others maintain the guard.

questions.questionText: According to the Hanafi Madhhab, what is the status of the Witr prayer?
options: Wajib (Necessary/Obligatory but slightly lesser than Fard)
questions.explanation: Hanafis consider Witr to be Wajib, requiring it to be made up (Qada) if missed.

questions.questionText: What distance (roughly) is generally accepted by the majority of scholars to allow shortening the prayer (Qasr)?
options: Any journey outside the city limits
questions.explanation: The majority set the minimum distance at 4 Burud, which translates to roughly 48 miles or 80 kilometers.

questions.questionText: If a latecomer joins the Imam just as he is rising from Ruku, what do they do?
options: Wait until the Imam stands up for the next Rak'ah
Join immediately but the Rak'ah does not count for them
questions.explanation: You should transition to whatever state the Imam is in, but missing the Ruku means that specific Rak'ah is not counted.

questions.questionText: Which scholar/school holds the strict view that reciting Surah Al-Fatihah behind the Imam in a loud prayer is NOT permissible?
questions.explanation: The Hanafi school holds that the recitation of the Imam is sufficient for the follower in all prayers.

questions.questionText: What is the ruling on praying in a garment containing a small amount of blood (less than a dirham coin)?
questions.explanation: A very small amount of unavoidable impurity (like a spot of blood less than a dirham) is excused in Hanafi Fiqh.

questions.questionText: How is Zakat calculated on business inventory (Urud al-Tijarah)?
options: Based on the original purchase price
Based on the expected future profit
Based on the current market wholesale value at the end of the Hawl
questions.explanation: Business inventory is evaluated at its current market value upon the completion of the Zakat year.

questions.questionText: What is the minimum Nisab for camels?
questions.explanation: Zakat becomes obligatory when one owns 5 camels, for which 1 sheep must be given.

questions.questionText: Regarding 'strong debts' (debts owed to you that you are confident will be repaid), when is Zakat due on them?
options: Only when the debt is finally collected
Every year as part of your total wealth
Only once after collection for the past years
questions.explanation: If a debt is 'strong' (the debtor acknowledges it and is able to pay), it is treated as wealth currently in your possession and taxed yearly.

questions.questionText: Is Zakat required on women's gold and silver jewelry meant strictly for personal adornment?
options: Yes according to Hanafi Fiqh, but No according to the majority (Jumhoor)
Only if the jewelry is inherited
questions.explanation: The Hanafis require Zakat on personal gold/silver jewelry if it reaches Nisab, whereas Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools do not.

questions.questionText: Are descendants of the Prophet's family (Ahl al-Bayt / Banu Hashim) eligible to receive obligatory Zakat?
options: No, it is strictly forbidden for them
Only if they are in extreme poverty
questions.explanation: Obligatory Zakat/Sadaqah is forbidden for the family of Muhammad (PBUH) as a matter of honor and purity; they may receive gifts instead.

questions.questionText: Can a person pay their Zakat in advance (e.g., for the next 1-2 years)?
options: Yes, it is permissible according to the majority if the Nisab is met
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) allowed Al-Abbas to pay his Zakat for two years in advance.

questions.questionText: What is the ruling on transferring Zakat funds from one's own city to another country?
options: Disliked unless there is a greater need (e.g., famine, war, poor relatives) elsewhere
questions.explanation: The fundamental principle is that Zakat should be distributed locally, but it can be transferred if there is a more pressing need elsewhere.

questions.questionText: Does an Waqf (Endowment) property itself require Zakat to be paid on its capital value?
options: No, because there is no specific human owner
questions.explanation: Waqf property belongs to Allah and does not have an individual owner, so there is no Zakat on the corpus/capital itself.

questions.questionText: Who are 'Al-Mu'allafati Qulubuhum' in the categories of Zakat recipients?
options: Those whose hearts are to be reconciled (e.g., new Muslims or potential allies)
questions.explanation: It refers to those whose hearts are drawn to Islam, often given to new converts or influential leaders to strengthen their faith or alliance.

questions.questionText: If one owns shares/stocks meant for long-term dividend investment (not trading), how is Zakat paid?
options: On the entire market value of the shares
On the dividend earnings only (like agricultural produce)
On the underlying zakatable assets of the company if discernible
questions.explanation: For long-term holdings, one pays Zakat on the proportionate zakatable assets (cash, inventory) of the company, or roughly 2.5% of the dividend if calculating assets is impossible.

questions.questionText: According to the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools, the severe penalty (Kaffarah) of fasting 60 consecutive days is explicitly for which act during a Ramadan fast?
questions.explanation: While Hanafis apply Kaffarah to eating/drinking intentionally as well, Shafi'is and Hanbalis restrict the 60-day penalty strictly to intercourse.

questions.questionText: What is 'Al-Wisal' in fasting?
options: Fasting continuously for days without breaking the fast at night
questions.explanation: Al-Wisal is continuous fasting without eating Iftar. The Prophet (PBUH) did this but forbade his Ummah from doing it out of mercy.

questions.questionText: What is the ruling on using an asthma inhaler (which contains aerosolized medicine) while fasting, according to contemporary major fatwa councils?
options: It does not break the fast, as it goes to the lungs, not the stomach
questions.explanation: The majority of modern scholars rule that inhalers do not invalidate the fast because the medicine acts on the respiratory tract, not the digestive system.

questions.questionText: If someone dies while owing obligatory fasts (e.g., from an illness they recovered from but didn't make up), what should be done?
options: Their heir (next of kin) can fast on their behalf
It converts to a financial debt only
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said: 'Whoever dies and owes some fasts, his heir should fast on his behalf.'

questions.questionText: According to the Maliki Madhhab, how often must the intention (Niyyah) for Ramadan be made?
options: Once at the beginning of the month for the entire month
It is not required at all
Only on the first and last day
questions.explanation: Unlike the majority who require a separate intention every night, Malikis allow a single intention for continuous required acts like Ramadan.

questions.questionText: Does cupping (Hijama) break the fast?
options: Yes in the Hanbali school, but No in the majority of schools
questions.explanation: The Hanbali madhhab holds that cupping breaks the fast for both the cupper and the cupped, while the majority say it only causes disliked weakness.

questions.questionText: If a pregnant or nursing woman breaks her fast purely out of fear for the health of her BABY (not herself), what is required of her according to the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools?
options: Both make up the fasts (Qada) and pay Fidya
questions.explanation: If the fear is solely for the child, they must make up the days and also pay Fidya (feeding a poor person) for each day missed.

questions.questionText: What happens if a person swallows vomit unintentionally while fasting?
options: The fast is broken, Qada is needed
The fast is broken, Kaffarah is needed
The fast is completely valid and unbroken
They must stop eating but the day doesn't count
questions.explanation: If one is overcome by vomiting unintentionally, the fast is not broken. Intentionally inducing vomiting breaks the fast.

questions.questionText: If a Muslim travels from a country that started fasting on a Monday to a country that started on Tuesday, and the second country announces Eid, but the traveler has only fasted 28 days, what must they do?
options: Fast on Eid day to make it 29
Celebrate Eid with the country they are in, then make up one day later
Ignore the new country and fast a 29th day normally
Nothing, 28 days is accepted for travelers
questions.explanation: A lunar month cannot be less than 29 days. They cannot fast on Eid, so they celebrate Eid with the locals and make up one day of Qada later.

questions.questionText: Which type of fast is considered 'Makruh Tahrimi' (Prohibitively Disliked) if done independently without joining it with a day before or after?
options: Fasting on the 13th of the month
questions.explanation: Singling out Friday for voluntary fasting is disliked unless it coincides with a habitual fast or is joined with Thursday/Saturday.

questions.questionText: What is the consequence of crossing the Miqat intentionally without entering the state of Ihram?
options: One must return to the Miqat to enter Ihram, or pay a Dam (sacrifice a sheep)
One just says Istighfar and continues
questions.explanation: Crossing the Miqat without Ihram requires the pilgrim to return to it. If they proceed, they must offer a Dam (penalty sacrifice).

questions.questionText: If a woman is menstruating, which pillar of Hajj must she delay until she is pure?
questions.explanation: A menstruating woman does all the rites of Hajj (including Arafah) except circumambulating the Kaaba (Tawaf).

questions.questionText: What is the ruling on 'Tawaf al-Wada' (Farewell Tawaf) for a menstruating woman leaving Makkah?
options: She must wait in Makkah until pure
It is completely waived/forgiven for her
She must pay a Dam instead
She performs it from outside the mosque
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) made an exemption for menstruating women, allowing them to depart Makkah without the Farewell Tawaf.

questions.questionText: For a pilgrim performing 'Hajj al-Ifrad' (Hajj only), what is the ruling on the animal sacrifice (Hadi)?
options: It is highly recommended (Sunnah) but not obligatory
questions.explanation: Unlike Tamattu' and Qiran where sacrifice is obligatory, a person doing Ifrad is not obligated to sacrifice an animal, though it is Sunnah.

questions.questionText: What is the primary condition for performing 'Hajj al-Badal' (Hajj on behalf of someone else)?
options: You must be related to them
You must have already performed your own obligatory Hajj first
You must do it for free
You must be older than them
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) heard a man making Talbiyah for 'Shubrumah' and ordered him to perform his own Hajj before performing it for Shubrumah.

questions.questionText: According to the majority of scholars (Jumhoor), what is the ruling of staying the night in Muzdalifah?
options: Fard (Pillar - Hajj is invalid without it)
questions.explanation: It is considered Wajib. If someone misses it entirely without a valid excuse, their Hajj is valid but they owe a penalty sacrifice (Dam).

questions.questionText: If a pilgrim in a state of Ihram hunts and kills a wild land animal, what is the required penalty?
options: Sacrificing a domestic animal of equivalent size/value, or feeding the poor, or fasting
Paying a monetary fine to the state
questions.explanation: The Quran dictates providing an equivalent livestock animal, or its value in food for the poor, or equivalent days of fasting.

questions.questionText: For women, what is the required amount of hair to cut to exit the state of Ihram (Tahallul)?
options: Cutting the length of a fingertip (Anmula) from the ends of the hair
questions.explanation: Women are forbidden from shaving their heads; they only gather their hair and trim roughly the length of a fingertip.

questions.questionText: If an elderly or sick pilgrim cannot throw the pebbles (Rami al-Jamarat) themselves, what is the Shar'i solution?
options: They may appoint a proxy (wakil) to throw the stones on their behalf
They wait until the next year
questions.explanation: Delegation is permissible for the stoning if a person is physically unable to reach the Jamarat due to extreme weakness or illness.

questions.questionText: What does 'Idtiba' refer to during the Tawaf?
options: Exposing the right shoulder by placing the Ihram garment under the right armpit and over the left shoulder
questions.explanation: Idtiba is the Sunnah for men of uncovering the right shoulder during the Tawaf al-Qudum (Arrival Tawaf) or a Tawaf followed by Sa'i.
